abstract_sentences.text: Diffusion policies have achieved remarkable success in robotic manipulation, yet they often fail to satisfy strict physical constraints required for safe deployment.
abstract_sentences.comparison: No explicit baseline; contrast is capability versus physical constraints.

evidence.anchor: often fail to satisfy strict physical constraints

abstract_sentences.text: Existing approaches impose safety either prematurely during training or reactively via external guardrails at test time, limiting policy expressivity and overall scalability.
abstract_sentences.comparison: Train-time safety is contrasted with test-time guardrails.
abstract_sentences.link_from_previous: Explains why the first sentence's gap persists.

abstract_sentences.text: We propose Physical safety Alignment for Constrained Trajectories (PACT), a self-evolving post-training framework that projects pretrained diffusion policies onto constraint-feasible regions without accessing demonstration data or task rewards.
abstract_sentences.comparison: PACT is positioned against approaches requiring demonstrations or rewards.
abstract_sentences.link_from_previous: Introduces the response to the stated gap.

abstract_sentences.text: PACT distills constraint gradients into the diffusion model through a reverse-KL objective with dense supervision across timesteps.
abstract_sentences.comparison: The supervision is per timestep rather than trajectory-level by description.

abstract_sentences.text: It incorporates a curriculum that progressively tightens constraints while maintaining theoretically bounded policy shift and monotone improvement, mitigating the safety-performance trade-off from catastrophic forgetting.
abstract_sentences.comparison: Curriculum is contrasted implicitly with abrupt enforcement.
abstract_sentences.link_from_previous: Adds the second mechanism and its proposed rationale.

evidence.anchor: bounded policy shift and monotone improvement

abstract_sentences.text: On simulated and real-world embodied manipulation benchmarks, PACT significantly reduces safety violations by 31.0% on average while improving task success by 30.7%.
abstract_sentences.comparison: Post-training PACT versus its base policies as summarized by the paper.
abstract_sentences.link_from_previous: Closes the abstract with aggregate empirical outcomes.

evidence.anchor: 31.0% on average while improving task success

abstract_summary: Function order is scope/problem, prior-work gap, core idea, two method mechanisms, then quantitative simulation-plus-real-world result. The abstract has no standalone limitation sentence; formal conditions and practical limitations appear later.

introduction_moves.first_sentence_role: Introduces diffusion-policy progress in robotic manipulation.
introduction_moves.open_question: Why can capable manipulation policies not be deployed safely?
introduction_moves.answer: Strict collision, force, and kinematic constraints are consequential.
introduction_moves.next_hook: Existing safety approaches are categorized next.

introduction_moves.first_sentence_role: Classifies design-time and test-time safety approaches.
introduction_moves.open_question: How do current approaches impose safety?
introduction_moves.answer: They require engineering/data or real-time guardrails/sensors and constrain expressivity or scalability.

introduction_moves.first_sentence_role: Frames post-training safety alignment as constrained projection.
introduction_moves.open_question: Why is post-training difficult for diffusion manipulation?
introduction_moves.answer: Diffused action mass, inaccessible demos/rewards, and catastrophic forgetting create three challenges.

evidence.anchor: First, diffusion models inherently spread probability mass

introduction_moves.first_sentence_role: Names PACT as a self-evolving post-training framework.
introduction_moves.open_question: What is the response to the three challenges?
introduction_moves.answer: Constraint distillation, self-rollouts, and curriculum updates.

introduction_moves.open_question: Does the method retain performance while improving safety?
introduction_moves.answer: The paper reports 31.0% fewer violations and 30.7% higher success.
No manual post-training data/test-time guardrail, curriculum distillation, and empirical gains.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 3.1
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Unlimited model capacity and sufficient data; fixed multipliers in the Lagrangian derivation.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Eq. (9) optimum is the score of the Eq. (7) tilted policy.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_correspondence: No direct finite-capacity theorem test; Tables 1-3 report outcomes.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem 3.3
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Each cost is bounded and the curriculum update is solved as specified.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Non-increasing expected Lagrangian cost and bounded KL policy shift.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_correspondence: Figures 4 and 13 are behavioral analogues, not direct measurements of the bound.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary 3.4
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Cumulative schedule eta_0=0 to eta_N=1 under the idealized assumptions.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Final curriculum solution coincides with Theorem 3.1 optimum.
equation_theory_inventory.empirical_correspondence: No direct validation of the closed-form distribution.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Theorem A.1
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Forward diffusion kernel and fixed multipliers.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Defines intermediate cost and score decomposition.

equation_theory_inventory.label: Lemma A.2
equation_theory_inventory.assumptions: Fixed state, nonnegative multipliers, normalized conditional density.
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Pointwise KL-Lagrangian minimizer is Boltzmann tilted.

evidence.anchor: Pointwise minimizer of the KL-regularized Lagrangian

equation_theory_inventory.label: Corollary A.3
equation_theory_inventory.conclusion: Expected total-variation bound scales with the curriculum increment.

experimental_design.name: Explicit research questions or preregistered hypotheses
experimental_design.description: No numbered research questions, preregistration, or decision rule appears in the PDF; contributions and ablations imply the questions.

experimental_design.name: Simulation task suite
experimental_design.description: RoboTwin bimanual tasks use randomized setup; Appendix C.2 defines seven tasks and their success conditions.

experimental_design.name: Base policies and adaptation
experimental_design.description: DP, DP3, RDT-1B, and pi0.5 cover distinct architectures, modalities, parameterizations, and samplers; DP/DP3 are fully fine-tuned and larger policies use LoRA.

evidence.anchor: base policies differ primarily in diffusion parameterization

experimental_design.name: Post-training data regime
experimental_design.description: PACT collects self-rollouts over 1,000 training scenes; 200 expert demonstrations are used to train/adapt base policies, not as stated PACT post-training input.

evidence.anchor: collects data by rolling out on 1,000 training scenes
200 expert demonstrations to train baseline methods

experimental_design.name: Constraint intervention
experimental_design.description: Three differentiable costs—poking, behavior alignment, rotation—are activated by task; simulation uses simulator state and real-world collection uses perception-derived information.

evidence.anchor: constraint activation is performed by a Vision-Language Model

experimental_design.name: Baselines
experimental_design.description: Baselines span off-policy IL/RL/distillation and on-policy IL/RL, including PLD, iDQL, AWR, QSM, DIPO, PPO, and online PLD/RFT variants.

evidence.anchor: learning paradigm (IL vs. RL) and data regime

experimental_design.name: Matched comparison conditions
experimental_design.description: On-policy methods are initialized from the same pretrained DP and matched in environment interaction and update budgets; Appendix C.7 repeats this protocol.

evidence.anchor: matched in environment interaction and update budgets

experimental_design.name: Outcome metrics
experimental_design.description: Success Rate measures completion; Safe Rate is the fraction of rollouts satisfying all demands. Appendix C.4 defines poking, falling, and toppling.

experimental_design.name: Real-world protocol
experimental_design.description: Four safety-critical tasks use a scaled-down instruction-free RDT; Appendix D evaluates 25 randomized trials per task and manually annotates safety/success under predefined rubrics.

evidence.anchor: Pour Water, Nail Insertion, Transfer Egg, and GPU Assembly
human annotators assess both safety and task success

experimental_design.name: Hyperparameters and hardware
experimental_design.description: Tables 7 and 12 provide schedulers, rollouts, epochs, optimizer values, and GPUs for simulation and real-world work; Tables 9 and 11 provide hardware/model details.

evidence.anchor: Hyper-parameter settings for real world evaluation

experimental_design.name: Random seeds and run-level replication
experimental_design.description: The PDF describes randomized scenes/placements but does not state seed counts, seeds, independent run counts, or run-level aggregates.

experimental_design.name: Data leakage control
experimental_design.description: The PDF distinguishes training scenes and evaluation episodes but does not give a dedicated leakage-control statement or holdout split specification.

evidence.anchor: 1,000 additional scenes from the training set

experimental_design.name: Failure decision
experimental_design.description: A rollout is unsafe if it triggers poking, falling, or toppling; real-world success uses task-specific point rubrics.

evidence.anchor: count a trial as safe only if none

experimental_design.name: Deployment boundary
experimental_design.description: Perception/VLM-based constraint construction is run only during data collection; deployment uses the base policy's regular onboard observation and no guidance injection.

claim_closure.claim: PACT can align policies post-training without demonstrations, task rewards, or test-time guardrails.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (9) and Algorithm 1 use self-rollouts; Appendix B puts cost construction in collection rather than deployment.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Simulation setup describes self-rollouts; Appendix B describes regular-observation deployment.

evidence.anchor: without accessing demonstration data or task rewards

claim_closure.claim: Reverse-KL score distillation recovers the constrained projection optimum.
claim_closure.method_response: Eqs. (5)-(9) define the projection, tilted optimum, teacher, and distillation target.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Theorem 3.1 and Appendix A.3 prove coincidence under stated idealized conditions.

claim_closure.claim: Curriculum distillation prevents catastrophic forgetting through bounded policy shifts and monotone improvement.
claim_closure.method_response: Eqs. (10)-(11) form the curriculum teacher from the prior policy.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Theorem 3.3 gives conditional Lagrangian/KL results; Figures 4 and 13 show smooth versus collapsing trajectories, but no empirical KL/TV bound is measured.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 says controlled shifts mitigate forgetting.

claim_closure.claim: PACT improves safety, task success, and training efficiency relative to shown baselines.
claim_closure.method_response: Dense per-timestep constraint gradients and few-step approximation are presented as mechanism.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1-3 and Figures 4/14 provide point estimates and curves across stated tasks/policies; no run-level uncertainty appears.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 says extensive simulation and real-world experiments demonstrate simultaneous improvements.

claim_closure.claim: PACT has meaningful real-world safety-critical performance, including GPU assembly.
claim_closure.method_response: The student policy absorbs constraint guidance before deployment.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 5/8 and Appendix D report four tasks with 25 randomized trials per task and manual rubrics; Pour Water uses a geometric proxy.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 cites safety-critical embodied manipulation scenarios.

claim_closure.claim: Deployment has no additional test-time overhead and is scalable.
claim_closure.method_response: Teacher costs are amortized into a student diffusion policy.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Appendix B.1 says collection-only perception/VLM and base-equivalent onboard deployment; Table 14 gives non-paired timing context, not fleet-scale evidence.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Section 5 calls the approach practical and scalable.

limitations.name: Upstream perception dependence
limitations.description: Alignment quality is coupled to vision/perception reliability; occlusion and ambiguity can propagate into safety supervision.

limitations.description: Self-evolving rollout collection adds computation despite no deployment-time overhead.

limitations.name: Geometric/kinematic scope
limitations.description: Current formulation focuses on geometric and kinematic constraints; high-frequency dynamics and force-sensitive contact remain future work.

limitations.name: Dual-use and misspecified constraints
limitations.description: Stronger manipulation policies can be misused or deployed under misspecified/adversarial constraints; the paper describes alignment as risk reduction, not formal guarantee.

final_judgment.single_storyline: PACT treats post-training safety as reverse-KL projection onto a constraint-feasible policy set, distills an implicit cost-gradient teacher on self-rollouts, and schedules the constraint strength to control intermediate policy shift.【pp. 3-5, §3, Eq. (4)-(14); explicit/interpretation】
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The body retains the problem, formal objective, implicit teacher, Algorithm 1, theorem statements, Tables 1-3, core ablations, and real-world headline; these are all on pp. 1-9.【pp. 1-9; layout_observation】
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, intermediate-cost derivation, costs, task rubrics, hardware, hyperparameters, collapsed-baseline curves, noise robustness, and low-data results are moved to Appendices A-E. This leaves mechanism legible in the body while proof validity and evaluation denominators require the appendix.【pp. 15-37; explicit/interpretation】
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 2 plus Eqs. (7)-(11) and Algorithm 1 form a compact target-distribution -> implicit-teacher -> self-rollout-training loop; Figures 3 and 13 supply the direct-distillation failure contrast.【pp. 4-5, 34; interpretation】
final_judgment.largest_gap: The conditional theorems assume unlimited capacity, sufficient data, bounded costs, and exact update behavior; experiments do not measure the stated KL/TV bounds and report no run-level uncertainty. Real-world pouring also uses a geometric proxy.【pp. 4-5, 19, 29-31, 34-37; explicit/layout_observation】
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For a claim that safety preserves capability, keep the safety target, update rule, a counterfactual failure mode, paired safety/task outcomes, and conditions in one main-body causal chain; relegate exhaustive configuration to the appendix.【pp. 4-9; interpretation】
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: This rule fits differentiable constraints with rollouts and paired safety/task metrics. It does not establish comparable conclusions when constraints are untrustworthy, perception is unreliable, or force/high-frequency safety is required.【pp. 9, 21-22, 32; explicit/interpretation】

lexical_rhetoric.count_scope: Exploratory searchable text from pp. 1-9 split before References; counts include abstract/captions and may retain table residue, so they are not the repository's canonical token counts.
lexical_rhetoric.contexts: Propose/introduce cluster in Abstract, Introduction and Method; evaluate/compare/report cluster in Experimental Setup, results captions, and ablations; the sole exact 'we find' introduces the curriculum ablation on p. 8.
lexical_rhetoric.segmentation_risks: safe includes Safe Rate/safe region/safety cost; policy includes base/student/optimal; table labels such as Succ. and formula fragments should not be treated as prose frequency.
